source.title: UniFork: Exploring Modality Alignment for Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation
source.authors: Tengtao Li; Quan-Feng Lu; Li-Rui Zhao; Hao Li; Xi-Zhou Zhu; Yu Qiao; Jun Zhang; Wen-Qi Shao

record.tranche_reason: Extends modality-alignment analysis to image understanding and generation in unified multimodal models, and compares the reported alignment trends on Geneval and MJHQ-30K inputs.
record.gate_note: The study measures image-text mutual-kNN alignment across layers and describes the resulting trends. It does not measure convergence between independently trained models as model capability or scale increases. The Geneval and MJHQ-30K analyses are reported as having consistent trends; exact alignment values are shown only in figures. Performance benchmark results are not rows because they do not measure representation alignment.
record.test_reason: The study borrows the mutual-kNN alignment metric from the Platonic Representation Hypothesis paper. It uses it to measure image-text token alignment across layers inside single models (LlamaGen, LLaVA-1.5, Emu3 variants, UniFork), in order to motivate an architecture. It never compares representations of independently trained models. It does not relate alignment to scale or capability, and it does not vary the metric or its settings. No version (V1–V7) names this within-model, layerwise, task-dependent construct. Repeating the analysis on MJHQ-30K checks whether the authors' own layerwise trend is robust. It does not test whether cross-model convergence depends on metric or data, so it does not bear on V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude that understanding and generation show divergent layerwise modality alignment patterns, and that fully shared backbones force a representational compromise. UniFork's Y-shaped shared-then-branched design accommodates both patterns and outperforms fully shared models.
record.recipe_differences: Uses mutual-kNN modality alignment, but analyzes within-model image-text features across layers and task settings; it does not test cross-model convergence with scale or capability.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported alignment trend is checked on Geneval and MJHQ-30K; the paper says the trends remain consistent despite the longer MJHQ-30K prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: Within-model image-text mutual-kNN alignment depends on task. In generation it rises then falls across layers; in understanding it increases monotonically. In jointly trained Emu3-base the two curves nearly overlap, while the task-specific fine-tunes recover distinct trends. These patterns hold on both Geneval and MJHQ-30K prompts, and UniFork's branches reproduce the expert trends. All values are shown in figures only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layerwise cross-modal alignment inside a multimodal transformer depends on the training objective (understanding vs generation), and joint next-token-prediction training yields a compromise trajectory.

record.problems: The alignment results are presented in figures without tabulated numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The analysis uses one stated similarity measure and does not compare its settings or test out-of-distribution inputs. It does not relate alignment to model scaling or measured capability.

untested.parts: No cross-model alignment as models get larger or more capable.
No alignment between separate vision and language models as both improve. The image-text alignment measured is within one model, across layers.
No mapping or stitching between models.
No interpretable features compared across models.
No variation of the similarity metric, the value of k, or out-of-distribution inputs for cross-model convergence. The two-dataset check concerns within-model trends only.
No measure of how complete cross-model alignment is, whether it plateaus, or what causes it.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 label was internally inconsistent: it was labeled 'challenges' while its reason described support. It is dropped because no row bears on V6. Performance benchmarks are correctly excluded from the rows.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test alignment between independently trained models as model size or capability increases.
Measures image-text features within task models across layers, not whether independent vision and language models align more as both improve.
Does not compare seeds or test shared features or subspaces across independently initialized networks.
Does not test mapping, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired interchangeability between models.
Does not test whether interpretable features or circuits recur across models.

Tests whether reported alignment trends persist across Geneval and MJHQ-30K inputs. It does not compare alternate similarity metrics, kNN settings, or out-of-distribution data, nor establish whether absolute alignment values depend on these choices.
Does not measure cross-model alignment completeness or plateau, or distinguish a shared model of reality from shared data or objectives as causes of cross-model convergence.
